title: Despite pain, two former October 7 Hamas hostages promote message of peace
subhead: Among the 251 Israelis taken captive by Hamas on October 7, 2023, Aviva and Keith Siegel chose to speak publicly about the abuse they suffered. While Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has claimed the release of hostages as an achievement in his election campaign, the couple in their 60s has continued to oppose the war.

subhead: As the budget debate approaches, La France Insoumise MP Eric Coquerel presents a strikingly high assessment of the consequences of the summer's extreme temperatures, aiming to build a stronger case for increasing funds allocated to adapting the country to climate change.

title: In Aberdeen, Scotland, the slow twilight of North Sea oil and gas
subhead: The British capital of black gold stands at the center of the United Kingdom's heated debates over how quickly to move away from fossil fuels. The city is eagerly awaiting a potential green light from the government to begin developing two new fields, one oil and the other gas.

title: Annick Lemoine, president of the Musée d'Orsay: 'I want the museum to become a place for debate that fosters critical thinking'
subhead: The new president of the museum dedicated to 19th-century art wants to attract a younger audience, she explained in an interview with Le Monde, and to draw connections between works from the past and contemporary social issues.

title: Why French high schoolers are protesting, and why their movement is already historic
subhead: What began as a spontaneous protest in the Paris suburbs has grown to a scale unseen in decades, as students denounce learning conditions and uncertain prospects. The government's essentially repressive response risks fuelling further anger.

subhead: The French health authorities reported that 8,124 deaths were related to the extreme heatwaves between late May and late August in France. Le Monde spoke to the friends and families of 11 of the victims to find out about the lives behind those numbers.

title: Anastasiia Yasagashvili, the Ukrainian collaborator who betrayed her family to the Russians
subhead: Sentenced to 15 years in prison for high treason, Anastasiia Yasagashvili collaborated with Russian forces after her village was occupied, before becoming a double agent. The investigative case file she provided to Le Monde reveals the journey of a young woman who had lost her way, for whom the war became a playground that fueled her love of adventure.
